articleTitle: Automatic recognition of plant leaves diseases based on serial combination of two SVM classifiers
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper presents a machine vision system for automatic recognition of plant leaves diseases from images. The proposed system is based on serial combination technique of two SVM classifiers. The first classifier uses the color to classify the images; it considers, at this phase, that the diseases with similar or nearest color belonging to the same class. Then, the second classifier is used to differentiate between the classes with similar color according to the shape and texture features. The tests of this study are carried out on six classes of diseases including three types of pest insects damages (Leaf miners, Thrips and Tuta absoluta) and three forms of pathogens symptoms (Early blight, Late blight and Powdery mildew). The results of the study show the advantages of the proposed method compared to the other existing methods.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of AODV routing protocol in MANET under the influence of routing attacks
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In the recent years, lots of research are going on in the area of Mobile Ad hoc NETworks (MANETs). This network is infrastructure-less network where nodes communicate with each other without any aid of centralized administration. Unfortunately, this feature causes the network vulnerable to various types of attacks. Hence, it is a challenging task in front of researcher to find out the suitable remedy to conciliate attacks in routing protocols. In this paper, we simulate black hole, flooding and rushing attacks which are threats in Ad hoc On-demand Distance Vector (AODV) routing protocol to analyze their impacts on this protocol using NS-2 network simulator. Previous researches take only one attacker or just the network size or the mobility to test their performance analysis, however, in this security analysis, we take into consideration the network size, the mobility, the traffic load and finally the number of the attackers. We use packet delivery ratio, average end-to-end delay and throughput as performance evaluation metric. Our simulation results show that the black hole attack have a severe impact on the network performance while the flooding and rushing attacks have less significant effect on the network performance.

articleTitle: ECG signals classification using MFCC coefficients and ANN classifier
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Recently, the detection of cardiac pathologies from the electrocardiogram, i.e. recording the electrical activity of the heart muscle, requires the use of more accurate tools for signal processing and decision making. In this context, this paper presents the design of a cardiac pathologies detection system with high precision of calculation and decision, which consists of the Mel Frequency Coefficient Cepstrum algorithms like fingerprint extractor (or features) of the cardiac signal and the algorithms of artificial neural network multilayer perceptron type multilayer perceptron classifier as fingerprints extracted into two classes: normal or abnormal. The design and testing of the proposed system are performed on two types of data extracted from the MIT-BIH database: a learning base containing labeled data (electrocardiogram normal and diseased) and another test base containing non- labeled data. The experimental results have shown that the proposed system combines between the respective advantages of the descriptor Mel Frequency Cepstrum Coefficient and the Multilayer Perceptron classifier.

articleTitle: Comparison of classification methods to detect the Parkinson disease
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Parkinson's disease is a chronic neurological degenerative disease affecting the central nervous system responsible for essentially progressive evolution movement disorders. The detection of this disease is made using a clinical diagnosis made by an expert. To save time and for more comfort in the Diagnostic and also to increase the efficiency of treatment through preventive detection, classification has found its place in the detection of this disease. For this purpose, many classification algorithms were used to achieve the best results, but the problem is which classifiers may be the most efficient for this detection, because each classification algorithms was applied to a local database, what influences the results. In this paper we have tried to apply three types of classifiers, k-near neighbor "k-NN", the Naive Bayes "NB" and support vector machines "SVM", on the same database to compare and to know which of the three classifiers will be the most efficient.

articleTitle: Adaptive ECG Wavelet analysis for R-peaks detection
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The Electrocardiogram has been established as a powerful diagnostic tool in medicine which provides important information about the patient's heart condition. The feature extraction of ECG such as R-peak detection is highly useful in cardiology. Continuous Wavelet transform based methods present best performance as irregularity measures and makes them suitable for ECG data analysis. In this work we propose a new method for R-peak detection based on continuous wavelet coefficients. The core of our method is to select automatically the analysis scale corresponding to maximum energy of ECG signal instead to consider all scales. In order to validate this method we apply it to several from apnea's database records. This new algorithm can be used to extract other features of ECG signals.

articleTitle: Backstepping control of a Doubly Fed Induction Generator integrated to wind power system
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper deals with the modeling and backstepping control of Double-Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) integrated into a wind power system. The proposed algorithm combines the nonlinear Backstepping approach and the field orientation applied to control the DFIG. In a first step, this technique is applied to the side converter rotor (RSC), to control the electromagnetic torque and reactive power, and secondly, it is applied to the grid side converter (GSC) to control the power exchanged with the grid and regulate the DC bus voltage. Simulations results present the performances in terms of set point tracking, stability, and robustness with respect to sudden changes in wind speed.

articleTitle: Design of temperature and humidity sensors for an electronic nose used in rotten food
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Food production has the major objective to achieve a high and uniform level of quality for raw materials. Temperature and humidity are the critical parameters to verify in many fields of food industry processes, from assurance of quality during production up to storage and transport to final users. In this regard, we focus in this paper on the design of temperature and humidity sensors for an electronic nose used to detect the rotten food in anticipation phase. Those parameters (temperature and humidity of food) have an important role in the array sensor of our nose.

articleTitle: Analysis and comparaison of different Heat Transfer Fluids for a 1MWe Parabolic Trough Collector
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The present work contains a numerical simulation of a 1MWe parabolic trough solar collector using 6 various Heat Transfer Fluids (HTF) under the weather conditions of Oujda (Morocco). Our objective is to study the performances of different HTFs and make a comparison between them in order to find out the most suitable HTF to be used for small scale solar plants. The main results of the simulations show that the VP1 is the best one to be used in this conditions, since it's the one that provide the highest thermal and electrical production that reach 650MWth and 200MWe in June respectively. However, the Molten Salts (Hitec and Solar Salt) are the disproportionate ones because the lowest thermal and electrical production.

articleTitle: Feature selection and parameter optimization of support vector regression for electric load forecasting
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Forecasting of future electricity demand has become a promising issue for the electric power industry. Since many factors affect electric load data, machine learning methods are useful for electric load forecasting (ELF). On the one hand, it is important to determine the irrelevant factors as a preprocessing step for ELF. On the other hand, the performance of machine learning models depends heavily on the choice of its parameters. These problems are known respectively as feature selection and model selection problems. In this paper, we use the support vector regression (SVR) model for ELF. Our contribution consists of investigating the use the particle swarm optimization for both feature selection and model selection problems. Experimental results on two widely used electric load dataset show that our proposed hybrid method for feature selection and parameter optimization of SVR can achieve better results when compared with the classical SVR model while using feature selection and without using it.

articleTitle: Wind energy conversion system using DFIG controlled by back-stepping and RST controller
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper present a maximum power point tracking (MPPT), the modeling and control backstepping of Double-Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) integrated into a wind energy system. The objective is to apply this technique to control independently the active and reactive power generated by DFIG, and compared with RST controller. The system performance was tested and compared by simulation in terms of following instructions and robustness with respect to parametric variations of the DFIG.

articleTitle: Forecasting of PV power application to PV power penetration in a microgrid
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper treats the subject of Photovoltaic (PV) power forecasting. The power generated by a PV system is always nonlinear because of the variability of weather parameters such as solar irradiance and temperature. This variability present a major challenge in term of penetration of power into a microgrid plus the difficulty in control and management of grid. Moreover, to respond to all these equivocal, we use the forecasting applied to PV power which will injected into a grid. Many Approaches and strategies are found in the literature review, but the difficulty is how to find the convenient forecasting method to predict the power output of any PV plant. In this study we present the NARX model destined to predict the PV power.

articleTitle: Stator and rotor faults detection in Induction Motor (IM) using the Extended Kaman Filter (EKF)
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Accurate knowledge of stator and rotor resistance variations in an Induction Motor (IM) has received a lot of attention due to its significance in improving the performance of the Machine. The paper deals with the application of the Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) algorithm in the purpose of stator and rotor faults detection in IM. The hypothesis on which detection is based is that the apparent rotor (stator) resistance will increase when a rotor bar breaks (shorted stator-turns). Mathematical model of the extended state estimator is presented, in which, the stator and rotor resistances are added as additional electromagnetic state variables.

articleTitle: Application of Li-Fi technology in the transmission of the sound at the base of the PWM
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Wireless communication is the need of the hour, so there is a huge thirst for improvement of the means of communication. Motivated by the looming crisis of radio frequency (RF) spectrum, light fidelity (Li-Fi) which is a technology attached to the visible light communications (VLC) offers many key advantages and effective solutions to the problems posed in the last decade. Through this technology, data is transmitted by light thanks to the unique properties of white light emitting diode (LED) lamps switching. In this article, we created a scheme of transmission at the base of the pulse-width modulation (PWM). The information that we are going to transmit in our case is an audio signal generated by a mobile phone. We create a sawtooth signal that we compare with our audio signal in order to create a PWM signal. Then this modulated signal will be transmitted by LED in the form of a light signal that the photodiode (PD) detects and transforms it into an electrical signal. Finally, we demodulate the signal obtained by a simple first-order low-pass filter RC to receive the demodulated in the speakers and therefore the maximum frequency of the transmission is 87 KHz.

articleTitle: Comparative study between two Maximum Power Point Tracking techniques for photovoltaic system
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study between two algorithms techniques which are Incremental Conductance and Perturb and Observe used to maximize the efficiency of the solar generator under variations of solar irradiation, temperature and electrical loads. Indeed, the Maximum Power Point Tracking algorithms are used to control a DC-DC boost converter to generate the Maximum Power Point of the generator photovoltaic. The computer simulation results, in Matlab/Simulink environment, presented in this paper show that the photovoltaic simulation system can track the maximum power point accurately using the two maximum power point tracking techniques.

articleTitle: Detection and identification algorithm of the S1 and S2 heart sounds
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This article attempts to contribute to heart abnormalities detection by suggesting a segmentation algorithm of S1 and S2 heart sounds. It describes the steps followed and the results achieved during the realization of the first PASCAL (Pattern Analysis, Statistical Modelling and Computational Learning) Classifying Heart Sounds Challenge. The performed work leads to improved results, compared to the results found by the three finalists of this challenge, using the envelope of Shannon energy and other methods, to detect and identify first and second heart sound of phonocardiogram signals.

Author Keywords: first Pascal Classifying Heart Sounds Challenge

articleTitle: Direct torque control of permanent magnet synchronous motors in MATLAB/SIMULINK
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper describes an investigation of the direct torque control (DTC) for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive. It is proven by equations that the increase of electromagnetic torque is proportional to the increase of the angle between the stator flux and the rotor flux linkage. The use of permanent magnet synchronous motor combined with direct torque control offers many opportunities such as quick, robust response and high-performance operations, which is desired for servo and traction applications in electric vehicles and wind turbines. In this paper, an overview is given. The basic principles of DTC for PMSM are explained. In addition, the estimations of stator flux linkage, torque and initial rotor position are needed in control scheme. To verify the feasibility of this scheme, simulation on SIMULINK is carried out. The results show an excellent characteristics for torque response and efficiency.

articleTitle: FPGA based real-time lane detection and tracking implementation
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this article, we present a system for robust lane detection and tracking. The proposed algorithm has two main parts. The first one is for lane detection using the Sobel operator with an adaptive threshold and the Hough transform, and the second part deals with lane tracking using the Kalman filter. To meet real time requirements, we use gradient directions of edge stage to simplify CORDIC algorithm. The obtained results show that the proposed algorithm can reliably detect and track lanes in different illumination condition.

articleTitle: Delay-dependent robust anti-windup synthesis approach to AQM in TCP/IP networks
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: An anti-windup compensator for input saturating systems with input and state delays is applied to active queue management (AQM) of a congested TCP/IP router. A TCP model with link capacity disturbances, modeling uncertainties and time-varying delay is investigated, and the objective is to design a controller which is capable of achieving the queue size and can guarantee robust stability in the presence of disturbance and model perturbations. Numerical example is given to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in comparison with other conventional methods.

articleTitle: Ground penetrating radar hyperbola detection using Scale-Invariant Feature Transform
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Ground-penetrating radar (GPR) is a geophysical method used for subsurface targets identification. However, a sophisticated processing of GPR data is necessary to extract targets signature.

articleTitle: Integral backstepping control based maximum power point tracking strategy for wind turbine systems driven DFIG
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this paper, a new robust and efficient nonlinear speed control strategy of the turbine-doubly fed induction generator system is designed in order to improve the control and the energy performances of this system. The proposed integral backstepping control includes two control blocks: the first one uses the MPPT strategy to adapt the turbine speed at the generator speed value by keeping the power coefficient at maximum value. The second block ensures the active and reactive powers generator regulation via control of dq-axis currents. The stability of the closed-loop system is analyzed and sufficient conditions are given to prove the practical stability. The simulations realized in Matlab/Simulink show the exploitation of the MPPT strategy, a good pursuit of the references and good stability.

articleTitle: Review: Linear, nonlinear and intelligent controllers for the inverted pendulum problem
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The pendulum is the most known mechanism of everyone. This is due to its importance historical and also to the number of the invention based on its operating principle. The inverted pendulum is an unstable system perfectly described by a nonlinear model obtained by applying the laws of physics. The design goal of the control law is to stabilize the pendulum in its upright unstable equilibrium position. In this article, a review of the different control law that have been applied to the system of the inverted pendulum with a cart is presented. And a comparison of each controller are discussed.

articleTitle: On-line signature verification using point pattern matching algorithm
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Authentication of persons has been known as a paramount part in society. Security requirements have given biometrics much attention. Verification of the signature is one of the biometric methods used in recognition systems. This paper presents a new method to verify an online signature of a person. In features extraction step, local parameters are extracted as time functions of different dynamic properties. In recognition phase the Discrete to Continuous Algorithm is applied on features to verify the signature claimed by a person. The results obtained by the proposed algorithm show a good accuracy rate.

articleTitle: UWB thin film flexible antenna for microwave thermography for breast cancer detection
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: A novel low-cost flexible antenna for a non-invasive and highly sensitive method to detect malign tumors in the early stages, contributing to diminishing the mortality which appears in the cases where the breast cancer was detected in late incurable stages. Using thin film Kapton substrate the flexible antenna has been built and carried out by the use of CST Microwave Studio software. The proposed structure operate in S-band (with reflection coefficient (S11) below -10dB) and has an ultra-wide band (UWB) characteristic providing an important bandwidth of about 2,4 GHz with a center frequency around 3 GHz. In order to predict the effect of the human body on the S-parameter response of the developed antenna design, an inhomogeneous multi-layer model of the women breast is used. The simulated results indicate that the proposed antenna kept it UWB property. The overall size of the miniaturized antenna is 20mm×22mm which make it very suitable for a radar-based breast cancer detection system.

articleTitle: Detection and classification of broken rotor bars faults in induction machine using K-means classifier
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Diagnostics of broken rotor bars fault in induction machine can be accomplished by analyzing the anomalies of machine local variable such as magnetic flux, stator current and neutral voltage signature analysis. This paper presents an accurate approach for modeling and simulating the dynamic behavior of the induction machines (IM), including rotor bar fault, and presents an advanced technique to detect and classify the broken rotor bars faults in (IM). The techniques used here are based on vector quantization method (k-means). This detection and classification are based on motor current signal analysis (MCSA). The presented structure manifests promising results using experimental and simulation data of stator current; under variable load, using the FFT approach for identification of the predominant frequency components and using the (K-means) approach for classification and class detection.

articleTitle: Improved license plate localization
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this article, a new approach to explore the candidate car license plate scene is presented. First, the image is decomposed by using a Haar wavelet to get the HL sub-image with vertical edges. Next, a black top-hat algorithm is applied to minimize the effects of interfering large continuous features other than the license plate. Then, the horizontal and vertical projections of the HL sub-image provide an approximate location of the license plate. The experimental results show the high precision of the proposed technique, with a success rate of 98% for parked vehicles and 97% for moving vehicles.

articleTitle: An empirical study of WIFI security and performance in Morocco - wardriving in Rabat
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Morocco is an important regional ICT player that offers interesting investment opportunities to many national and international companies. It is important for these companies to have a good understanding of network performance and security in Morocco. Unfortunately, however, most prior work on network performance and security is interested in countries other than Morocco. In this paper, we perform a field study of WIFI networks in Rabat, the capital of Morocco, using wardriving. Our study covers about 10,000 WIFI networks in residential and administrative neighborhoods in Rabat. We find that 77% networks use WPA or WPA2, indicating that WIFI security in Morocco is comparable to WIFI security in developed countries. We also find a balanced use of channels 1, 6, and 11 indicating that network operators are aware of high interferences that can occur on channel 6 and therefore act to minimize interferences. Overall, our results indicate that WiFi situation in the Rabat neighborhoods examined is very encouraging.

articleTitle: Big Data: Framework and issues
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Nowadays, many industries and governments around the world are experiencing unprecedented increase in the volume, variety and velocity of information, due to the deployment of the new generations of mobile networks, increased use of smartphones, the explosion of numbers of subscribers, the multitude of services offered, online transactions and the rise of social media. These massive data is considered a gold mine that must be tapped to enjoy, to do this, Big Data proves the most appropriate technology.

articleTitle: Sliding mode controller using nonlinear sliding surface applied to the 2-DOF helicopter
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Control of the helicopter includes nonlinearities, uncertainties and external perturbations that should be considered in the design of control laws. This paper presents a control strategy for TRMS (twin rotor mimo system), based on the sliding mode control using non linear sliding surfaces. The choice of this algorithm was justified by his robustness with respect to modeling errors and external disturbances. The simulation results of the proposed algorithm control show good performances. Finally simulation results are included to indicate the TRMS system with the proposed controller can greatly alleviate the chattering effect and remain a good trajectory tracking.

articleTitle: Extreme learning machine for fault detection and isolation in wind turbine
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a new scheme for fault detection and isolation (FDI) in variable speed wind turbine. The proposed scheme is based on an intelligent data-driven fault detection scheme using the extreme learning machine approach (ELM). The ELM is a kind of single hidden layer feed-forward neural network (SLFNN) with a fast learning. The basic idea is the use of a certain number n of ELM classifiers to deals with n types of faults affecting the wind turbine. Different parts of the process were investigated including actuators and sensors faults. The effectiveness of the proposed approach is illustrated through simulation.

articleTitle: Automating Data warehouse design using ontology
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Requirement Analysis is a crucial and arduous task in data warehouse design process. We provide a solution to support data warehouse design, which combines need driven and data driven design approaches. Our solution is based on ontology representation language and work results on ontology alignment. Our design method occurs in two steps. The first one, which is interactive and semi-automatic, transforms user requirements into ontologies, the second step that is fully automatic, aligns the resulting ontologies from the first step and produces an ontology associated to the Multidimensional Data model. The waste management field will be our guideline to illustrate our approach.

articleTitle: Directional communications with smart antenna system to improve energy efficiency in wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The capacity of wireless sensor network (WSN) can be severely limited due to interference constraints. The integration of smart antenna system (SAS) in wireless sensor networks is a challenging and very attractive technical solution to improve the system capacity, the quality of service, and the power control. Smart antenna system has the advantage over traditional omnidirectional antennas system (OAS), of being able to orientate signals into the desired direction in either transmission node or reception node. In this paper, we create a view of ground with nodes by using MATLAB, firstly nodes composed with OAS and secondly nodes composed of SAS, then we compare active communication using SAS and active communication using OAS. The energy efficiency to bring by smart antenna system is described.

articleTitle: High-level performance estimation of image processing design using FPGA
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: We propose a methodology for an early performance estimation of FPGA-based image processing applications. Using UML activity diagram of an application, each operator is decomposed into operational units with fine to medium granularity. Elementary operations are modeled experimentally in terms of latency, power and area to form a pre-characterized operators library. The results demonstrate that performance estimation at a very high abstraction level is already possible with an error less than 5%, and that the estimations are highly correlated to the results obtained in the final implementation.

articleTitle: Using RASTA-PLP for discriminating between different Neurological diseases
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The aim of this study is to discriminate between patients with Parkinson's disease and patients who suffer from other Neurological disorders by analyzing voice recordings in cepstral domain. The technique used in this study is to extract cepstral coefficient of ReAlitive SpecTrAl PLP (RASTA-PLP). The extracted RASTA-PLP cepstral coefficients were compressed by calculating their average value in order to get the Voiceprint from each voice recording. For classification, we used Leave one subject out validation scheme along with SVM supervised learning classifier. The best obtained accuracy was 85%.

articleTitle: Fuzzy logic based impoved direct power control of three-phase PWM rectifier
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this paper we propose an approach to improve the direct power control (DPC) of three-phase PWM based on fuzzy logic technique switching table. The fuzzy DPC controller presents the advantage to be based on linguistic description, the controller ensures a good regulation of the dc-bus voltage, active and reactive power-flows of the grid connected converter by selecting the optimum state of the rectifier and guarantees the power factor close to one. The steady state and dynamic behavior of fuzzy DPC (FDPC) is presented that illustrate the operation and the performance of the proposed method. To test the fuzzy control strategy a simulation platform using MATLAB/SIMULINK was built, simulations have been made to illustrate the performance of the presented control strategy.

articleTitle: Comparative study of topology-based routing protocols in vehicular ad hoc network using IEEE802.11p
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Vehicular ad-hoc network (VANET) is a new environment in wireless networks that facilitate communication between auto-mobiles. VANET is the most known approach for the intelligent transportation system (ITS) that has the main aim to improve the road safety and provide passengers comfort. Therefore, many researchers are interested more than usual in this area of wireless and mobile communications in order to implement new approaches. The most issues in this field are in providing VANET routing protocols in high speed environment. In this paper, we describe the principal characteristics and discuss the research challenge of topology-based routing in this type of networks. We also compared this kind of routing protocols in VANETs on the basis performance metric in two standards of mac protocols IEEE802.11 and IEEE802.11p using NS2.

articleTitle: Integral sliding mode control without reaching phase for a variable speed wind turbine
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this paper, sliding mode controller (SMC) and integral sliding mode controller (ISMC) are designed for a variable speed wind turbine. The main objective of the controller is to optimize the energy captured from the wind at below rated power. To overcome the steady state error, the ISMC is introduced. However, in the presence of large uncertainties, ISMC control approach produces oscillatory phenomenon due to the higher needed gain. To eliminate the tradeoffs between the ISMC tracking performance and the high gain at the control input, we have introduced a new method based on the modification of the output tracking error through the use of the exponential function in order to eliminate the reaching phase. The stability of the proposed ISMC is analyzed by Lyapunov theory and the control action didn't show any chattering. The simulation results of ISMC are presented and the control performance is compared with conventional SMC.

articleTitle: Modeling and simulation for ideal and real photovoltaic module which fed water pumping system with nonlinear integral Backstepping Controller
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper suggests a comparison between two cases of new control strategy in order to track the maximum power point of a PV water pumping system. The first case represents the photovoltaic panel without series and shunt resistances. The second case the photovoltaic panel system with a series and shunt resistances. The solar panel is connected to the DC motor pumping by using a DC-DC Boost converter. The suggested strategy is based on the integral Backstepping control design to be utilized on the DC/DC converter in order to realize an optimal power output of the PV array. The integral action is inserted to raise the robust control properties of nonlinear Controller. The algorithm controls the stability via analysis of Lyapunov. The performances approach and system developed has been analyzed and compared with the simulation model that was based in Matlab/Simulink environment to illustrate the validity of the control method in the two cases.

articleTitle: Fingerprint matching algorithm based on discrete to continuous approach
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Matching is a key operation in the current fingerprint system. The objective of fingerprint matching is to achieve a high reliability in comparing two fingerprint details. The large variability in different impressions of the same finger makes reliable matching fingerprint an extremely difficult problem. In this paper, a minutiae-based algorithm for fingerprint pattern recognition and matching is proposed, based on discrete to continuous approach, which is essentially a point pattern matching approach. By transforming this discrete problem to a continuous problem, the experimental results of the proposed algorithm demonstrate efficient recognition and matching performance compared with several minutiae based algorithms.

articleTitle: Detection and localization of the open circuit fault using the park's approach: An overview
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper presents a new approach for open circuit fault diagnosis using the park's vector technique in a three phase voltage source inverter. The technique has proved its effectiveness through simulation results, the standard deviation of the currents in the d-q frame was used to extract the symptoms failure, and the analysis of the currents to localize the faulty switch, within one current period and half without additional sensors which reduce the costs, a fault tolerant system was also proposed.

articleTitle: MRAS and Luenberger observers using a SIFLC controller in adaptive mechanism based sensorless fuzzy logic control of induction motor
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Most industrial applications require high performance speed sensorless operation and demand new control schemes in order to obtain fast dynamic response. In this paper, we present a comparison between MRAS and Luenberger observers based fuzzy logic control SIFLC type. We also present a speed sensorless fuzzy logic control (SIFLC) of induction motor (IM). This command is a powerful tool to reject disturbances. However, the chattering phenomenon presents a major disadvantage for variable structure systems. To reduce this problem, a saturation function is used to limit chattering effects. MRAS and Luenberger observers based on fuzzy logic adaptive mechanism are designed for speed estimation. These proposed schemes will allow a large reduction in computation time of such a drive and thus facilitate its implementation. Numerical simulation results of the proposed schemes illustrate the robustness against load torque disturbances and the good performance of sensorless induction motor.

articleTitle: The impact of MAC protocols in energy consumption of transferring multimedia contents using Castalia simulator
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Wireless Sensor Network is a technology that allows the ability to exchange information and all kinds of files wirelessly, and It can be deployed in different environments. There is also a more sophisticated material which can record and transmit different types of data, such as sound, video and image. Thus, In order simulates the multimedia transfer we use a simulator instead of a real experiment. We choose to use the simulator Omnet++/Castalia and use a video sensor model with OMNET++ because it's a complete and tested model for transferring images on the raw. Also, we will test the effect of the MAC protocols on energy consumption and the quality of the transferred images in Omnet++/Castalia by using Opencv to transform images from the spatial space to a frequency space.

articleTitle: Highly efficient error correcting codes for ubiquitous healthcare in Wireless Body Area Networks
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper presents an improved architecture for Wireless Body Area Network (WBAN) communication systems in health-care monitoring environment. Due to the anatomy of the human body, the WBAN communication can encounter heavy noises and the signal will be significantly jammed. For small scale WBAN networks, it's much more difficult to correct the faulty data and erroneous information captured at the receiver. In order to overcome the noisy environment of the WBAN communications, we construct a static XOR based architecture with three relays selection to improve the redundancy in the small scale network and force the encoding and decoding operation to be more and more efficient. The proposed architecture is based on linear block codes, over the Rician fading channel environment. The obtained results show that the improved architecture performs better over Rician channel and has very good results in term of Binary Error Rate (BER).

articleTitle: Seven views + one
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Process modeling is of paramount importance in organization. It is a powerful tool to manage and control all its activities. However, the diversity of approaches and standards proposing process modeling makes choosing a methodology for modeling processes a delicate work. This choice has become more difficult, given the increasing complexity of current information systems and requires the consideration of several aspects and dimensions. This paper proposes to explore a new way for modeling business processes within a complex environment, and defines an extension of the seven views approach by adding a system dimension. This extension, based on the System of Systems paradigm, provides to designers and project managers a multi-level view (system / subsystems) by expliciting the relationship between processes and complex system.

articleTitle: Low-cost Maximum Power Point Tracking structure of a grid connected wind conversion chain based on a PMSG
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper provides a complet structure of Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) consisting of a variable speed wind turbine, a drive train, a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator PMSG, electronic power converters connected to the grid. To achieve the maximum of generated power the MPPT principle is essential, it is based on the Perturb & Observe (P&O) algorithm. To reduce cost of the structure by avoiding speed sensors, the adopted MPPT strategy is based on sensorless wind speed, air density and turbine parameters, and generates the output used to control the buck. Then a regulation is realised for the grid side in order to control the inverter and a PLL is used to synchronize the frequency of the inverter voltages with that of the grid voltages. At first, we show the complete chain and detail its components. Then we describe the speed estimator used and the chosen method to design a sensorless MPPT. Simulation results can be found at the end of this paper, confirming the performance of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: An ontology-based framework for virtual enterprise integration and interoperability
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Virtual enterprise integration and interoperability between its different information systems are the first systemic paradigms to achieve a successful collaborative product development. In such a context, the information flow has a centric place. Therefore, our aim in this paper is to propose a new ontology-based framework, exploiting the expressiveness of ontologies to ensure collaboration and semantic interoperability between partners and using, at the same time, ontologies inference capacities to support the decision making processes. An industrial application will be developed in the context of the simultaneous design of products and their optimized supply chains.

articleTitle: Review of recovery techniques to recapture lost targets in wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Target tracking, which is one of the most important applications in wireless sensor networks, has received considerable attention in the last few years. The main objective of Object tracking sensor network (OTSN) is to track single or multiple targets and report their latest location to the application's user. However, these targets may get lost due to several reasons such as presence of obstacles or holes in the network, sudden changes in the target's trajectory, localization and prediction errors. This can be a crucial issue in sensitive applications like the military field. To overcome such problem, efficient and strong approaches are needed to retrieve the lost target in a timely manner. This article reviews some recovery strategies proposed in literature, and discusses the main reasons that result in target losses. Then the paper provides a detailed analysis and comparison between these strategies.

articleTitle: Multiple zonal approach for clustered wireless sensor networks
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In wireless sensor networks (WSN), energy consumption is a major factor that alter the metric of network life time. Reducing energy consumption during communication between nodes is a major issue to consider in designing a wireless sensor network. A vast majority of WSN routing protocols are focusing on energy efficiency. Clustering remains the most efficient routing approach used in WSN. However, latterly, clustering algorithms have shown their limitation in extending the network lifespan. Some clustering approaches in wireless sensor networks require impartial spread of dissipated energy in order to prolong the lifetime of sensor node. In this paper, we proposed a new clustering approach MZ-LEACH based on multiple triangle zones distribution and LEACH protocol. The proposed approach creates properly multiple partitioned triangle zones and provides appropriately a well cluster heads repartition in the network in order to improve the communication efficiency between cluster heads and the base station. Simulation results In MATLAB tool show that the proposed approach ameliorates the network lifespan and minimizes the energy consumption of the sensor nodes. An efficiency comparison of the proposed approach with LEACH protocols is performed.

articleTitle: Optical liquid sensor based on periodic multilayers structure
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: We introduce a liquid refractive index sensor based on a one-dimensional photonic crystal formed by alternating layers of Barium fluoride (BaF2) and Gallium arsenide (GaAs) with an empty layer in the middle. This lamellar cavity (defect layer) will be filled with polluted water. We demonstrate the device through the selective infiltration of a single layer with liquid along a photonic crystal. The numerical results show that the frequency of the peak caused by the impure water is sensitive to water-liquid mixture. The sensor achieves very high sensitivity. A detection limit of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-5</sup> refractive index units has been derived from measurements with a sensitivity of 1480nm per refractive index unit.

articleTitle: The control strategy for a hybrid wind-photovoltaic system with compressed air storage element
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this recent years, the global energy demand increases more and more, and the increasing scarcity of fossil energy sources in the near future is predictable, so the progress of renewable energy especially solar and wind become increasingly competitive in terms of technology production and costs, the wind-solar hybrid systems permit offsetting the intermittent nature of renewable sources and provide a higher overall energy efficiency, their primary interest is the possibility of energy autonomy because they do not rely on a single source. They can solve a lot of energetic problems if they are associated with a storage system, the selected storage system is the storage form of compressed air (CAES: compressed air energy storage).

articleTitle: Neural network based electromagnetic torque identification of squirrel cage induction motor
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this paper, an electromagnetic (EM) torque identification scheme of squirrel cage induction motor (SCIM) using recurrent neural network (NN) model is developed. The searched parameters are estimated by using Levenberg-Maquart (LM) training algorithms, meanwhile its structure is optimized involving the Akaike final prediction error (AIC-FPE) criterion. To this end, a simulation model is elaborated to collect the required training input-output data. The benefits of this identification method are manifold: it is online, it is based on the measured data only, it takes into account the saturation and transient behavior, and it is very suitable for predictive control. The usefulness of the developed method is examined by simulation within an automotive application.

articleTitle: Towards an automatic assessment system in introductory programming courses
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Nowadays, automatic assessment of programming assignments has become an important topic in academic research. In fact, the increasing number of enrolled students in programming courses created the need of a system providing immediate feedback to the learners and saving teachers from manually managing all the students' solutions. This paper presents an attempt to conduct programming exercises assessment both dynamically and statically to ensure a reliable and objective evaluation job. While dynamic analysis is based on xUnit framework, the static analysis is performed on the graph representation of the programs.

articleTitle: A novel filter based on three variables mutual information for dimensionality reduction and classification of hyperspectral images
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The high dimensionality of hyperspectral images (HSI) that contains more than hundred bands (images) for the same region called Ground Truth Map, often imposes a heavy computational burden for image processing and complicates the learning process. In fact, the removal of irrelevant, noisy and redundant bands helps increase the classification accuracy. Band selection filter based on “Mutual Information” is a common technique for dimensionality reduction. In this paper, a categorization of dimensionality reduction methods according to the evaluation process is presented. Moreover, a new filter approach based on three variables mutual information is developed in order to measure band correlation for classification, it considers not only bands relevance but also bands interaction. The proposed approach is compared to a reproduced filter algorithm based on mutual information. Experimental results on HSI AVIRIS 92AV3C have shown that the proposed approach is very competitive, effective and outperforms the reproduced filter strategy performance.

articleTitle: High torque control performance utilizing a three level inverters with a simple switching strategy of induction machine
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The three level inverters (NPC), present a big interest in the field of the high voltages and the high powers of the fact that they introduce less distortion and weak losses with relatively low switching frequency. This paper present a direct torque control of three level inverters fed induction machine. In order to provide better torque regulation and lower switching frequency, a simple switching strategy was presented using seven level torque hysteresis and two level flux hysteresis controllers to give more options in selecting an appropriate voltage vector. Simulation results have proven a good performance and verified the validity of this approach using Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Online characterization of switched reluctance motors
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: An online characterization of switched reluctance motor (SRM) including the mutual coupling effects, magnetic saturation and parameters variation, is developed in this paper. The optimization of the SRM performances in terms of efficiency and high power density requires an accurate and less-complicated model. The model building can be used for simulation, control, and diagnosis purposes based on the observed phase currents, voltages and rotor position measurements only, which are accessible in normal operating regime, without need of any prior knowledge of the motor parameters. Compared to the existing methods, the developed characterization scheme is automatic, transparent to the vehicle passengers, and takes into account the trade-off between accuracy and complexity. The effectiveness of this method is demonstrated by simulation within an automotive application.

articleTitle: Velocity control of DC machine using multicellular power converter
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper focuses on the problem of controlling multicellular converter (three cells), in order to drive a DC machine, the control objectives is twofold, the first one is to regulate the voltage of the flying capacitor, the second is to regulate the speed of DC motor to a desired value. The whole system is described by 4th order nonlinear mathematical model and controlled by using the backstepping approach and tools from Lyapunov stability. The simulation results have been performed through Matlab/SimPowerSystems environment and show that the designed controller meets its objective.

articleTitle: Automation of access control negotiation in dynamic coalitions for electrical critical infrastructures
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Our national security, economic prosperity, and national well-being are dependent upon a set of highly interdependent critical infrastructures (CI). The need to share information in a secure way between collaborating CIs is becoming increasingly important, in order to benefit from shared applications and resources. Coalitions between autonomous domains are often formed to enable access permissions to shared objects based on negotiated resource-sharing agreements. The dynamic nature of coalitions, as member domains may leave and new ones may join, creates new challenges relative to security management. We distinguished the need for automating the process of access negotiation in dynamic coalitions. In this paper, we briefly review the recently proposed approaches and discuss the open issues.

articleTitle: A new approach to DWT design for real time de-noising of vibration signatures related to the induction machine defects
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Extracting only useful information for vibration monitoring from those sensed by an accelerometer decreases the amount of data to be transmitted and greatly reduces the size of required monitoring and diagnosis applications. This paper presents a suitable architecture for real time FPGA implementation of the discrete wavelet transform for extracting useful signatures of electrical machine defects. Based on wavelet bases selected in order to meet the specificities of these signatures, the implemented algorithm only uses a single pair of LUT-based filters controlled by an FSM. Design complexity and used resources are greatly reduced, while maintaining a very satisfactory execution rate.

articleTitle: A comparative study of simple clear sky irradiance models
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The production of a photovoltaic (PV) system is intrinsically linked to the amount of radiation it absorbs. The irradiance impinging on the PV system is an attenuated version of the clear sky irradiance. The degree of this attenuation depends on the level of cloudiness. In this paper, we address the problem of clear sky irradiance modeling. This irradiation can be correctly estimated if some atmospheric concentration components are known. However, these atmospheric data are not always accessible; they are very often unavailable or the cost of their acquisition is exorbitant. In this study, we undertook a comparative study of three simple clear sky irradiance forecasting models, which do not require such atmospheric data to be known. Their outputs were tested using a set of ground measurements performed at the solar farm of the International University of Rabat. The results of this comparison show that the best model provides a relative root mean squared error lower than 7%.

articleTitle: Planning a trajectory of a 6-DOF parallel robot «HEXA»
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The parallel structure robot with 6-DOF “HEXA” has found use in high-end systems when multiple degrees of freedom and large workspace are required. In this paper, we establish the inverse kinematic model of robot “HEXA” in order to follow various given trajectories. However, simulating robots is one of the essential elements of modern manufacturing plants, so in this work we plan simples and complexes trajectories, and we simulate the capacity of the robot to follow these trajectories in order to be efficient in planning tasks in parallel structures such as the legged robots.

articleTitle: Detection model based on multi-sensor data for early fire prevention
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this work, we adopt a model of making-decision applied in wireless sensor networks for environmental protection. This model applies firstly the Equal Gain Combiner rule for fusing data measured from sensors, chained to a classification by the K-nearest neighbors algorithm to provide an instant decision, this latter is evaluated later on a comparison to the Chair-Varshney rule. The results show that our approach is also reliable and stable in prediction and decision. Also, the advanced performance of our model in terms of processing speed relative to the Chair-Varshney rule.

articleTitle: Design of an MPPT control under asymmetrical grid faults of DFIG wind turbine
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study of wind turbine control based on Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) under unbalanced grid voltage using an Proportional-Integral (PI) and backstepping intelligent controllers. The traditional PI controller is more sensitive to the grid disturbances; however the simulation results showed that the backstepping design is characterized by a high rejection to the grid voltage perturbations. The objective of this control is twofold: ensure the achievement of maximum power point (MPPT) and regulate the rotor flux by controlling the stator reactive power. The validation of results has been performed through simulation using Matlab/Simulink®.

articleTitle: Reflectivity- losses compromise on the basis of a Bragg filter with high index modulation
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this article the authors explain the necessary compromise that should be attained between gain and losses by examining the impact of corrugation depth 1 on the reflectivity R and the losses of a Bragg Gratings-based optical filter, achieved by the technique of Focused Ion Beam (FIB). We demonstrate that if an optimal corrugation depth is achieved the filtering function of the device gets a high degree of performance. Indeed, we have been able to experimentally measure this (optimal) depth on several constructed structures and show that once the reflectivity reaches its maximum value, it is contre-productive to exceed this value of depth. In point of fact, we found out that going beyond this value causes an increase of the losses (related to the BG), and does not improve the reflectivity any further. The augmentation of losses degrades the transmission quality by giving rise to an increase of error probability and a lowering down of the bit rate.

articleTitle: Resolution of energy balance equations for cascade solar still using Matlab/SimulikTM
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The need for production of fresh water from brackish water is considerably high, especially in dry regions. In this paper a new approach to design of solar still absorber plate was developed and its effect on the productivity was investigated theoretically. A mathematical model was developed to calculate the theoretical productivity of the solar still. The energy balance equations for the various elements of the solar still are formulated and numerically solved; using the dynamic simulation program Matlab/SimulinkTM. The performance of the still was investigated. The results show that the thermal performance of a modified stepped solar still can be considerably improved through the new modification.

articleTitle: ANFIS modeling of nonlinear inductance
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Adaptive network based fuzzy inference system (ANFIS) is an intelligent neuro-fuzzy technique which has proven to be able to model and control of various nonlinear and uncertain systems. The research presented in this paper aims to develop a new original fuzzy model of single-phase HV power supply of microwave magnetron. The design of this system is composed of leakage flux transformer with magnetic shunts supplying a cell, which multiples the voltage and stabilizes the current and one magnetron at the output of the cell. An equivalent model of this transformer is presented taking account the characteristics of the magnetron. It is based on the development of a new diagram block of non-linear inductance, using the Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). This model was validated under MATLAB-SIMULINK© near the nominal state. The results obtained by simulation are in good agreement with experimental measurements.

articleTitle: Static behavior analysis of silicon carbide power MOSFET for temperature variations
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an analysis of the static behavior of a SiC-MOSFET power transistor for temperature variations. The commercial transistor model (CMF10120D Cree 1200V/24A) is used. The approach consists to exploit the Spice electrical model provided by the constructor and to set its limits. Two main parameters: the threshold voltage and mobility are investigated to meet the needs of the static study and refine the temperature behavior of the Spice model. The obtained simulation results are compared to experimental measurements achieved in a static athermal mode.

articleTitle: Study and design of a grid-connected single phase PEM fuel cell inverter
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this study, the control of the inverter power system and the fuel cell production system secured the main behavior of the distributed generation on the grid power injection. The deadbeat control strategy allows high control flexibility and capability of adapting to the network faults. Coupling and decoupling systems are provided ensuring the safety of the electric production and the electrical system under different conditions. The power injected to the grid has a low level of harmonics thanks to the filters used in power and control system.

articleTitle: Shadow detection and removal for traffic sequences
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper address the problem of shadow detection and removal in traffic vision analysis. Basically, the presence of the shadow in the traffic sequences is imminent, and therefore leads to errors at segmentation stage and often misclassified as an object region or as a moving object. This paper presents a shadow removal method, based on both color and texture features, aiming to contribute to retrieve efficiently the moving objects whose detection are usually under the influence of cast-shadows. Additionally, in order to get a shadow-free foreground segmentation image, a morphology reconstruction algorithm is used to recover the foreground disturbed by shadow removal. Once shadows are detected, an automatic shadow removal model is proposed based on the information retrieved from the histogram shape. Experimental results on a real traffic sequence is presented to test the proposed approach and to validate the algorithm's performance.

articleTitle: Wide band frequency lumped parameters equivalent model for power networks
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper presents a new dynamic equivalent model for distribution power networks using MATLAB SIMULINK. It is based on the representation of the medium power transmission line by π circuits. The method gives complete information about the dynamic behavior of the system. The distribution network is analyzed in a wide range frequency domain and the oscillations can be observed. The dynamical behavior of the network as a function of its input impedance is deduced. Application to an IEEE 37 test distribution feeder is presented and the extension of the model to a distributed parameters line is considered.

articleTitle: Features fusion for characterizing INBREAST-database masses
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this paper a novel technique of mass characterization based on robust features-fusion is presented. The proposed method consists of mainly four stages: (a) the first phase involves segmenting the masses using edge information's. (b) The second phase is to calculate and fuse the most relevant morphological features. (c) The last phase is the classification step which allows us to classify the images into benign and malignant masses. In this step we have implemented Support Vectors Machines (SVM) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), which were evaluated with the following performance criteria: confusion matrix, accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, receiver operating characteristic ROC, and error histogram. The effectiveness of this new approach was evaluated by a recently developed database: INBREAST database. The fusion of the most appropriate morphological features provided very good results. The SVM gives accuracy to within 64.3%. Whereas the ANN classifier gives better results with an accuracy of 97.5%.

articleTitle: A multi-channel cooperative MIMO routing protocol for clustered WSNs
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Energy efficiency and quality of service are foremost concerns in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs). Among the methods used to achieve these requirements there is virtual multiple input multiple output (MIMO) technique, where sensor nodes cooperate with each other to form an antenna array. These multiple antennas can be used to improve the network performance (lifetime, data rate, bit error rate ...) through spatial diversity or spatial multiplexing. In addition, multi-channel frequencies technique which represents recent communication standards like IEEE 802.15.4 can helps to improve network throughput and eliminate collision, idle-listening or overhearing, which are consequences of overconsumption energy. In this paper, we propose a distributed multi channel cooperative MIMO routing protocol for cluster based WSNs (MCMIMO) which aims to take both advantages of abovementioned techniques in order to further boost network performance in multi-hop WSNs. In MCMIMO, sensor nodes are organized into clusters and each cluster head utilizes a weighted link function to select some optimal cooperative nodes to forward or receive traffic from other neighboring clusters, furthermore different channels are assigned to adjacent clusters and cooperative MIMO links in order to reduce collisions. Simulation results indicate that our approach achieves a significant reduction in energy consumption and boost in network throughput.

articleTitle: Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna (RDRA) for anti-collision short range radar (SRR) application
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper presents the design of Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna (RDRA) feed by a micro-strip line for anti-collision radar SRR application at 24 GHz. The proposed RDRA operates at a frequency of 24 GHz with a high dielectric constant of 41. The simulated RDRA has a high radiation efficiency (88.4 %). The return loss, radiation pattern and gain of the proposed antenna are evaluated. The simulation process was carried out using Computer Simulation Technology (CST) Microwave Studio.

articleTitle: Study and analysis of a three-phase rectifier with Push-Pull control
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: In this paper, a study of a type “Boost” rectifier was carried out. Among the systems operating in discontinuous mode, the latter offers the ease of control and carry less important voltage on the semiconductor. However, since the input current is discontinuous, that increases the Electromagnetic Interference (EMI). So to meet the standards, an additional filter is necessary within a restricted power range. To improve the performance of this type of systems, we proposed a new configuration in which we included the command of two rectifiers ‘Push-Pull’. This technique allowed the system to face less pulsating currents, and therefore it enhances the filtering. Great importance was given to the modeling of this type of rectifier. The simulation results were presented taking into account the control loop. The performance of the new solution was evaluated using the electrical efficiency.

articleTitle: Multiple relaxation-time lattice Boltzmann heat transfer computation of channel flow past various bodies
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: A numerical investigation to simulate the fluid flow and heat transfer in a two-dimensional horizontal channel containing a multi heated physical rectangular bodies is conducted using hybrid thermal lattice Boltzmann method (HTLBM). A combination between the Multiple Relaxation Time-Lattice Boltzmann Equation (MRT-LBE) D2Q9 for fluid velocity and Finite Difference Method (FDM) for temperature is used. In the plane channel, the bodies are placed in a side-by-side arrangement and normal to the incoming flow. The air flow is assumed to be laminar and incompressible. Special attention is paid to investigate the effect of the Reynolds number on the fluid flow and the heat transfer, where the dimensions and the distance between the bodies are fixed.

articleTitle: Analysis of the single phase full bridge bidirectional boost rectifier via Singular Perturbation approach with power factor correction
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: This paper presents a single phase full bridge bidirectional boost rectifier with power factor correction. A novel control based on Singular Perturbation is used in this circuit to assert that inductor currents are fast states and capacitor voltages are slow states. The goals of this paper are the analysis and the design methodology of cascaded proportional-integral controller in feedback loop by using of the singular perturbation technique, that guarantees desired output transients where two-timescale motions are artificially induced in the closed-loop system. The stability analysis is based on the use of Lyapunov function. The stability of limit cycle in the fast dynamical subsystem gives the robustness of the output voltage value in the presence of external disturbance and the resistor load variations. The simulation results have been performed through Matlab/Simulink environment and show that the designed controller meets its objective.

Author Keywords: single phase full bridge bidirectional boost rectifier

articleTitle: Study of the safety fuzzy logic controller with 2003 architecture using the Reliability Bloc Diagram and the Fault Tree Analysis
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Analysis of a safety fuzzy logic controller implemented in Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) can be performed by different methods. These methods should comply with international standards (IEC 61508 [1] and ISA TR 84.0.0.2 [2]). This paper proposes a comparison between two safety fuzzy logic controllers both implemented in FPGA with 1002 and 2003 architectures. This comparison is based on a qualitative and a quantitative analysis provided by these standards. The quantitative analysis is performed by the calculation of average probability of failure on demand (PFDavg) of safety related systems to define it safety integrity level (SIL). The qualitative analysis is based on the Reliability Block Diagram method [3] and [4] and Fault Three Analysis [4] and [5].

Author Keywords: Average Probability of failure on demand (PFDavg)

articleTitle: Digital controller design for full-bridge Boost Rectifier using Singular Perturbation method based on pseudo continuous approach with power factor correction
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The systematic approach of designing a robust digital controller to solve output regulation problem for a full bridge boost rectifier with unknown external disturbances and varying parameters is discussed. The design of digital controller based on the so-called pseudo-continuous approach by using Singular Perturbation is presented, where this controller is the result of continuous-time controller discretization. In the paper the control scheme for full bridge Boost Rectifier begins with the assertion that inductor currents are “fast” states and capacitor voltages are “slow” states. This assertion must be true for power factor correction converter to allow independent control of current and voltage. The continuous-time controller using proportional integral approach in feedback is used, and the effect of discretization at discrete time instants has been taken into account by inclusion of a zero-order hold transfer function. The pseudo-continuous-time model of a control loop with the pure time delay is used to calculate the parameters of a digital controller, where the pure delay is a result of the zero-order hold transfer function approximation. Numerical simulation for full bridge boost rectifier in discrete mode is presented

articleTitle: Toward a Service Broker for telecom service integration in IMS network
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The world of telecommunications is undergoing a rapid change in designing and developing applications. Telecom operators are becoming increasingly forced to diversify the portfolio of available services to ensure customer loyalty. Indeed the operator's business has far exceeded the supply of traditional telephony to open up to the most demanding services. For this purpose IP Multimedia Subsystem (IMS) has been a major work effort of the 3GPP (3rd Generation Partnership Project) standards bodies for several years now. However, the acquisition of services by operators slows down the development of services offered because of the integration difficulties, and the quality of services issues. This has let to a new approach proposed in this paper. The idea is to set up a Service Broker (SB) able to look for the best offer of service requested to deliver it to the customer. To ensure a transparent communication between operators, customers and service providers, the NGOSS (New Generation Operations Systems and Software) Framework is used in a consistent manner.

articleTitle: A comparison of different methods for numerical analysis of heat transfer in a transverse channel
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: Forced convection in complex geometries is important in many industrial applications and especially in nuclear reactors, heat exchangers, solar collectors, cooling turbomachinery and electronics. In this paper we have tried to apply the finite volume method to the simulation of free surface flows to compare the solutions obtained by different patterns and compare with the exact solutions. This comparison allowed us to determine the reliability of the most precise pattern. In this communication, we will present, the physical problem of convection-diffusion and stationary within a horizontal channel follows. the mathematical formulation based in equation diffusion convection in one dimensional and the boundary conditions imposed on each size, are shown in detail.

articleTitle: A Faber Schauder dominant blocks based fragile watermarking scheme for image tamper detection
publicationTitle: 2016 International Conference on Electrical and Information Technologies (ICEIT)
abstract: The need of digital content authentication is increasing, due to the easier the digital content modification becomes, that is owing to the technology development. Several fragile watermarking based methods have been proposed to authenticate image. In such methods, a mark is embedded into the digital image to authenticate it. There is a few methods that deal with algorithm complexity, hence it can not be used for the applications that require low complexity such as real-time applications and video processing applications. We propose in this paper, a Faber Schauder dominant blocks based fragile watermarking scheme for image tamper detection. The Watermark was generated by applying Xor operation between a logo's bits and the bits of dominant blocks singular values of the image to authenticate. These dominant blocks are obtained by applying Faber Schauder Discrete Wavelet Transform (FSDWT) to that image. Since the image is characterized by its contours and its around textures which contain an important concentration of dominant coefficients -that form dominant blocks-, any image modification will result in a significant change of the dominant blocks singular values, which lead to detect the authenticity of the image.
